name: Mondrian
tagline: Java ROLAP engine that answers MDX queries by generating SQL against your relational warehouse.
description: Mondrian is a relational OLAP (ROLAP) engine written in Java. You describe cubes, dimensions and measures over existing star or snowflake schemas in an XML schema file, and Mondrian turns MDX queries into SQL against the underlying database, caching cell results and using aggregate tables when they exist. It exposes the olap4j API and XML for Analysis, powers Pentaho's analysis tools and has been embedded in other BI front ends. First released in 2002 and acquired by Pentaho in 2005, it is still developed in the pentaho/mondrian repository, but since Pentaho 10.3 (late 2024) the source has been published under the Business Source License 1.1 instead of the EPL. It is only a query engine: storage, durability and scale come from the SQL database beneath it.

license.name: Business Source License 1.1 (since 10.3; older releases EPL)

pricing.notes: Source is free for non-production use under BSL; production use needs a Pentaho commercial license. Each version converts to Apache 2.0 after four years.

scale.notes: Scales with the SQL database underneath; Mondrian itself is a JVM process with an in-memory cell cache.

strengths: Adds an MDX/OLAP layer over an existing relational warehouse without copying data
Aggregate-table awareness and a cell cache cut repeated query cost
Standard olap4j and XMLA interfaces for pivot-table clients
Two decades of production use inside Pentaho deployments
weaknesses: Speed is bounded by the SQL it generates and the database underneath
Verbose XML cube schemas are hard to maintain
Moved to BSL 1.1, so production use now requires a commercial license
MDX skills and client tooling are increasingly niche
useCases: Pivot-style analytics over a star schema in PostgreSQL, MySQL or a warehouse
Embedding OLAP cubes in Java BI applications
notIdealFor: Teams wanting a SQL-first semantic layer
Huge data volumes without a fast columnar database underneath
